_about.note: Evidence category of every RoverBalance field (Prompt 10, part 1: rover economy, salvage supply, garage). Categories: fictional (fictional game tuning supported by real principles: a stronger motor gives a higher top speed, more battery stores more energy, grip = friction coefficient x normal load, climbing energy = m g h, rolling resistance = c m g per metre; NOT NASA measurements of a crewed rover, and no register entry gives rover specifications), balance (game tuning with no source; never a NASA figure), map (read from data/colony_manifest.json), S01 (NASA NSSDCA Mars Fact Sheet, VERIFIED: mean surface gravity 3.73 m/s^2, used as RoverBalance.MARS_GRAVITY). The assembly check's numbers (voltages, amp-hours, wheel radii, example masses) are illustrative examples built from the same curves. Nothing here is presented as measured data.

top_speed_mps.note: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 m/s (10.8 to 25.2 km/h) for speed levels 1-5. More drive-motor power, higher top speed. Game tuning, not a rover specification.

motor_power_kw.note: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 kW for speed levels 1-5. Shown in the garage and used by the current check (current = power / voltage).

drive_force_n.note: 3000, 3700, 4400, 5200, 6000 N total wheel push for torque levels 1-5: climbing and pulling away with a load.

battery_capacity_kwh.note: 20, 28, 36, 46, 56 kWh for battery levels 1-5. A refit never fills the battery.

cargo_capacity_kg.note: 100, 175, 250, 350, 450 kg for cargo levels 1-5. Cargo capacity only: the rover has four seats in every build.

traction_mu.note: 0.45, 0.53, 0.60, 0.67, 0.75 tyre-to-ground friction coefficient for traction levels 1-5. Grip = this x normal load (principle); not a measured Mars soil value.

chassis_mass_kg.note: 1400 kg empty rover with level-1 modules.

battery_mass_per_level_kg.note: +40 kg per battery level above 1 (more modules).

cargo_frame_mass_per_level_kg.note: +20 kg per cargo level above 1 (stronger frame).

crew_member_kg.note: 150 kg per occupied seat (person, suit and pack). Game value.

rolling_resistance.note: 0.15: share of the weight that resists rolling on loose ground (principle: F = c m g). Not a measured Mars value.

drivetrain_efficiency.note: 0.8: battery-to-wheel share (motor, gearbox, wiring losses). Principle-based game value.

map_distance_factor.note: 60: every metre driven or climbed on the map uses the energy of 60 m. The playable map is about 150 m across; without this the battery would never matter. Like the short game sol, it is a game rule, and it does not change with the sol length setting.

range_terrain_factor.note: 1.3: the range estimate allows 30 % more energy than flat firm ground for slopes and soft sand. Range assumes the battery, cargo and crew aboard now (at least a driver) and no energy back downhill.

charger_kw.note: 5 kW taken from the colony battery while charging (the colony battery holds 700 kWh in GameBalance at V1, since 2026-11-14).

charger_efficiency.note: 0.9: share of the charger's energy that reaches the rover battery (the colony battery's own charge efficiency is also 0.9 in GameBalance).

charge_radius_m.note: 7 m cable reach from the charger station (the parked rover's centre is 3.1 m from it).

charge_reserve_fraction.note: 0.35: charging pauses at 35 % of the colony battery (above the 30 % low-battery warning), or at the energy_battery_reserve upgrade's life-support reserve if higher.

rover_reach_m.note: 6 m from the rover's centre to get in, load or unload: half its 6.2 m length plus the 2.6 m interaction reach (same as data/rover.json enter_distance_m).

garage_radius_m.note: 6 m: the rover counts as in the garage (for assembly and refits) within this distance of the garage station.

item_mass_kg.note: supply_crate 25 kg, sample 2 kg. Game values.

salvaged_part_kg.note: 12 kg per salvaged part. Game value.

default_item_kg.note: 10 kg for any other item. Game value.

park_position.note: (8.3, 0, 23.0): sf_rover's origin, Blender (8.3, -23.0, -0.00136) in data/colony_manifest.json. Used until data/rover.json gives the garage park pose.

park_yaw_deg.note: +90 degrees: sf_rover's rotation in the manifest (its headlights FX_sf_rover face +x, towards the garage door).

seat_offsets.note: Fallback seat points in the rover's frame until data/rover.json (vehicle part) gives the real ones.

exit_offsets.note: Fallback exit points beside the rover (they fall in the 1.45 m gaps between the parked rover and the garage walls, from data/colliders.json) until data/rover.json gives the real ones.

challenge_max_stats.note: At most 3 changed modules are checked in one assembly or refit, biggest change first, so the check stays short.

example_voltages.note: 96, 120, 144 V: battery voltages the assembly-check examples use (illustrative).

example_wheel_radii.note: 0.4, 0.5 m: wheel radii of the torque examples (illustrative).

supply_demand.note: Spare parts supply against demand (checked against the data files by tests/test_rover.gd). Supply = start + one spare part per recovered donor part (refurbish + bench test, the P08 flow). The P08 rule ScienceBalance.parts_per_donor lets each donor give 1 part, or 2 after the res_component_refurbishment upgrade (which itself costs 2 parts), whatever the number of compatible parts it lists.
supply_demand.flag: SHORTFALL: the approved damaged objects can supply at most 40 parts (10 at the start + 30 recovered from 15 donors, incl. the scout update's broken-down rover) against 102 for every card, every comms stage and a fully upgraded rover. A fully upgraded rover alone (50) is not reachable, even if nothing else is bought. The campaign needs only 1 part (comms_radio_1; sector tiers cost no parts, and the rover can be assembled at level 1 for 0 parts), so the campaign is not blocked. No debris was spawned. Owner decision needed (see NOTES.md).

donors_not_used.note: Candidates checked in the manifest and not made donors: mb_crash_cart (a medical emergency 'crash cart' in the Med Bay, working equipment, not wreckage); ls_manifold (the working life-support manifold; nothing marks it damaged); ex_lander (the intact spacecraft standing on the landing pad, 28 m tall: the crew's arrival vehicle); rf_tile_*_dead (6 dead ceiling tiles 3.0-4.7 m above the floor, out of reach); hb_rover (the hangar rover, parked on chocks with its charge cable: not derelict); hg_kiosk_dark (its screen is lit; 'dark' is its colour).
